entries.effect: 1 when /AS or /V names the widget's ON-STATE, or when BOTH name a state that is not /Off; and -1 for a widget that is not a BUTTON.  Three clauses over 31 measured shapes, and the on-state is -buttonWidgetStateString's answer. entries.effect: the BACKGROUND colour of a WIDGET, off /MK's /BG, in the DEVICE colour space the array's COMPONENT COUNT names - one is DeviceGray, three DeviceRGB and four DeviceCMYK (PDF 1.7 Table 8.40) - with the ARRAY'S OWN components and an ALPHA OF 1, which CGColorCreate wants as one value past the space's component count and which a PDF colour array does not carry.  Nothing converts.  Read by the seam revenant_annotation_background_colour in RevenantPDFKitColours.h over 48 named fixtures: [1 0 0] answers DeviceRGB 1, 0, 0, 1; [0.5] DeviceGray 0.5, 1; [0 0 0 0] DeviceCMYK 0, 0, 0, 0, 1 - a CMYK colour of four zeros and NOT white; [0.1 0.2 0.3 0.4] the same space unchanged; (a string) nil; a /Btn answers DeviceRGB 0, 0, 1, 1; and /MK carrying /BC [1 0 0] beside /BG [0 1 0] answers the /BG.  A /Ch widget with no /Opt is NOT SURFACED AT ALL, by -[PDFPage annotations]' choice-widget skip - which is what an earlier version of this row mistook for a /Ch answering a green its array does not contain: that green was the NEXT annotation's /BG, read one index out of step.

entries.effect: the /DA's FIRST fill operand, and only a fill one, in the GENERIC colour spaces rather than device ones. Read by the seam revenant_annotation_font_colour over the position, operand-count and no-/DA fixtures: `0 g` answers kCGColorSpaceGenericGray 0, 1 and `1 g` the same space at 1, 1; `1 0 0 rg` answers kCGColorSpaceGenericRGB 1, 0, 0, 1; both CMYK values answer the gray default, so k is not read either, and so do all three STROKE operands - which is the format's own rule and not a gap, because text is painted with the fill colour.  The operand's POSITION does not decide, being FIRST does: `0.5 g 1 0 0 rg` answers the gray and `1 0 0 rg 0.5 g` the RGB.  A colour operator with the wrong operand count is not refused but reads the numbers in front of it, so `0.5 0.25 g` answers 0.25.  An annotation with NO /DA and a /DA with no readable fill are TWO DIFFERENT DEFAULTS, the gamma 2.2 gray and the gamma 1.0 one. The three colour-space NAMES are API_AVAILABLE(ios(9.0)) in this SDK against a row whose minimum is 6.0, and the port binds them anyway: CoreGraphics exports kCGColorSpaceGenericGray, kCGColorSpaceGenericRGB and kCGColorSpaceGenericCMYK from 3.0 and kCGColorSpaceGenericGrayGamma2_2 from 4.0 (tools/cache-index/first-rung.lua), and all four are in the 4.3 AND the 6.1.3 armv7 caches' own CoreGraphics export tries, read through tools/corpus/cache-value.lua.  So the annotation is the header's and not the export; the import is weak under this deployment target, the gate checks that it resolves, and there is no availability test and no fallback.

entries.effect: the /DA's font NAME and SIZE, read INDEPENDENTLY of one another, by the seams revenant_annotation_font_name and revenant_annotation_font_size.  Three clauses over 24 fixtures: the name AS WRITTEN when -[UIFont fontWithName:size:] has a font of that name - /Courier answers Courier, and /Helvetica-Oblique and /Times-Roman answer themselves; else an EXACT table of THREE abbreviations, Helv to Helvetica, HeBo to Helvetica-Bold and Cour to Courier; else HELVETICA.  All fourteen abbreviations of the standard fourteen are measured and the other eleven answer Helvetica, which is a fact about PDFKit and not about the format - PDF 1.7 9.6.2.2 has /TiRo as Times-Roman and it does not.  The table is exact and case-sensitive: /H, /Co, /Ti, /HELV and /Hebo all answer Helvetica.  -[NSFont fontWithName:] is nil for all fourteen, so this is PDFKit's own table and not the platform's lookup.  The SIZE is kept whatever becomes of the name - /Nonexistent 9 Tf answers Helvetica at 9 - and defaults to 12 when the /DA carries none, which is what every annotation without a /DA answers.
